clues: This town sits on a high flat plain in Ecuador. It lies south of Quito, where two small rivers join into one.
High peaks with snow sit close by, so the air here stays cold. Winds sweep over the bare flat land where it stands.
This town was first built in 1534, long ago. Earthquakes then broke it down four times in the years that followed.
The live volcano Cotopaxi stands close to this town. It has erupted again and again, and each blast hurt the town.
This town is famed for a dish with a fun name, chugchucaras. Cooks also serve plantains, popcorn, and toasted corn.
